<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0in">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; width: 100%">
<TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<TD STYLE="text-align: justify; width: 0.25in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>2.1</B></FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify; width: 0.25in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>&nbsp;</B></FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Nature of Business Acquired</B></FONT></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0pt">On August 28, 2026,
the Company completed its previously announced acquisition (the &ldquo;<B>Acquisition</B>&rdquo;) of all of the issued and outstanding
shares of GeoPura Limited (&ldquo;<B>GeoPura</B>&rdquo;) by the Company&rsquo;s wholly-owned subsidiary (the &ldquo;<B>Buyer</B>&rdquo;)
pursuant to a share purchase agreement dated June 23, 2026 (the &ldquo;<B>Purchase Agreement</B>&rdquo;) entered into between, among
others, the Company, the Buyer and those persons whose names and addresses are set out in Schedule 1 thereto (the &ldquo;<B>Sellers</B>&rdquo;).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0pt">GeoPura, founded
in 2019 and headquartered in Newcastle, United Kingdom, is a provider of zero-emission, hydrogen-based power solutions. GeoPura designs,
manufactures, operates, leases and sells its Hydrogen Power Units (&ldquo;<B>HPUs</B>&rdquo;), which use the Company&rsquo;s fuel cell
modules to convert hydrogen into electricity and provide clean, low-noise, off-grid power. GeoPura also produces green hydrogen, generated
via electrolysis, at its dedicated production sites, including through its 50% ownership interest in UK-based HyMarnham Power, and holds
a contract under the UK government&rsquo;s inaugural Hydrogen Allocation Round 1 (HAR1), a subsidy mechanism guaranteeing hydrogen production
revenues over fifteen years.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; width: 100%">
<TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<TD STYLE="text-align: justify; width: 0.25in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>2.2</B></FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify; width: 0.25in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>&nbsp;</B></FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Acquisition Date</B></FONT></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0pt; color: blue">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">August
28, 2026.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0pt; color: blue">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; width: 100%">
<TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<TD STYLE="text-align: justify; width: 0.25in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>2.3</B></FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify; width: 0.25in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>&nbsp;</B></FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Consideration</B></FONT></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0pt; color: blue">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">Consideration
for the Acquisition consisted of (i) upfront consideration of &pound;269.6 million (the &ldquo;<B>Upfront Consideration</B>&rdquo;),
being the headline purchase price of &pound;275.0 million as adjusted in accordance with the terms of the Purchase Agreement, and (ii)
contingent consideration of up to &pound;27.5 million (the &ldquo;<B>Contingent Consideration</B>&rdquo;) payable in cash and/or shares
pursuant to the terms of the Purchase Agreement if GeoPura achieves certain specified financial milestones following the closing of the
Acquisition (&ldquo;<B>Closing</B>&rdquo;). Any Contingent Consideration that becomes payable may be satisfied, at the Company&rsquo;s
sole discretion, in</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0pt; color: blue">&nbsp;</P>




<!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 1 -->
    <DIV STYLE="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt; border-bottom: Black 1pt solid"><P STYLE="text-align: center; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">&nbsp;</P></DIV>
    <DIV STYLE="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><P STYLE="text-align: center; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">&nbsp;</P></DIV>
    <!-- Field: /Page -->

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">cash, through the issuance of common shares of the Company at a price per share equal to the 30-day trailing volume-weighted average price
of the common shares on the business day immediately preceding the applicable payment date, or a combination thereof. Any cash portion
of the Contingent Consideration is expected to be funded from the Company&rsquo;s cash on hand.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 1in; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0.5in; text-align: justify">The Upfront Consideration was satisfied
on Closing through a combination of: (a) a cash payment of &pound;77.1 million (the &ldquo;<B>Closing Payment</B>&rdquo;), funded from
the Company&rsquo;s cash on hand; (b) the issuance of 49,584,212 common shares of the Company (the &ldquo;<B>Consideration Shares</B>&rdquo;)
to the Sellers at a deemed price of US$5.02 per share, based on the Company&rsquo;s 30-day volume-weighted average share price prior
to the date of the Purchase Agreement (the &ldquo;<B>30-Day VWAP</B>&rdquo;); and (c) the grant of 1,084,540 rollover restricted share
units (the &ldquo;<B>Rollover RSUs</B>&rdquo;) under the Company&rsquo;s GeoPura Restricted Share Unit Plan (and not under the Company&rsquo;s
existing Consolidated Share Distribution Plan) in consideration for the release and cancellation of certain GeoPura options held by GeoPura
optionholders. The Rollover RSUs represent 1,084,540 common shares of the Company reserved for issuance, having a deemed issue price
of US$5.02 per share based on the 30-Day VWAP, and are expected to vest twelve months following Closing. The Consideration Shares and
the common shares underlying the Rollover RSUs represented approximately 14.1% of the Company&rsquo;s outstanding common shares on a
pro forma basis. For accounting purposes, the Consideration Shares and the Rollover RSUs are measured at their estimated fair value as
of Closing, based on the closing price of the common shares on the date of Closing, and the total preliminary purchase consideration,
including the estimated fair value of the Contingent Consideration, is approximately US$230.7 million, as described in the unaudited
pro forma condensed consolidated financial statements attached as Appendix C.</P>

<P STYLE="text-align: left; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 12pt"><B>Independent
Auditor&rsquo;s Report to the Members of GeoPura Ltd</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: center; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: left; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">To
the Board of Directors of GeoPura Ltd.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: left; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Opinion</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">We have audited the consolidated financial statements of GeoPura Ltd (&lsquo;the group&rsquo;), which
comprise the consolidated statement of financial position as at 31 March 2026 and the consolidated statements of loss and comprehensive
loss, the consolidated statements of changes in equity/(deficit), the consolidated statements of cash flows for the year then ended and
the related notes, including a summary of significant accounting policies. The financial reporting framework that has been applied in
their preparation is applicable law and International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRSs) as issued by the International Accounting
Standards Board.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">In our opinion the accompanying financial statements present fairly, in all material respects the consolidated financial
position of the group as at March 31, 2026 and its consolidated financial performance and its consolidated cash flow for the year then
ended in accordance with IFRSs as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Basis
for opinion</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">We conducted our audit in
accordance with International Standards on Auditing (&lsquo;ISAs&rsquo;) and applicable law. Our responsibilities under those standards are further
described in the &lsquo;Auditor&rsquo;s responsibilities for the audit of the financial statements&rsquo; section of our report. We are independent of
the group in accordance with the ethical requirements that are relevant to our audit of the financial statements in the United Kingdom,
including the Financial Reporting Council&rsquo;s Ethical Standard and we have fulfilled our other ethical responsibilities in accordance with
these requirements. We believe that the audit evidence we have obtained is sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for our opinion.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Responsibilities
of directors</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">The directors are responsible for the preparation and fair presentation of the financial statements in
accordance with IFRSs as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board, and for such internal control as the directors determine
is necessary to enable the preparation of financial statements that are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">In preparing the financial statements, the directors are responsible for assessing the group&rsquo;s ability to continue as a going concern,
disclosing, as applicable, matters related to going concern and using the going concern basis of accounting unless the directors either
intend to liquidate the group or to cease operations, or have no realistic alternative but to do so.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">The directors are responsible for
overseeing the Group&rsquo;s financial reporting process.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Auditor&rsquo;s
responsibilities for the audit of the financial statements</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">Our objectives
are to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements as a whole are free from material misstatement, whether due
to fraud or error, and to issue an auditor&rsquo;s report that includes our opinion.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">Reasonable assurance is a high level of assurance, but
is not a guarantee that an audit conducted in accordance with ISAs will always detect a material misstatement when it exists.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">Misstatements
can arise from fraud or error and are considered material if, individually or in the aggregate, they could reasonably be expected to
influence the economic decisions of users taken on the basis of these financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Extent
to which the audit was considered capable of detecting irregularities, including fraud</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">Irregularities, including fraud, are instances of non-compliance with laws and regulations.
We design procedures in line with our responsibilities, outlined above, to detect material misstatements in respect of irregularities,
including fraud. The extent to which our procedures are capable of detecting irregularities, including fraud is detailed below. However,
it is the primary responsibility of management, with the oversight of those charged with governance, to ensure that the entity&rsquo;s
operations are conducted in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and for the prevention and detection of fraud.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: left; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: left; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 12pt"><B>Independent
Auditor&rsquo;s Report to the Members of GeoPura Ltd (continued)</B></FONT></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: left; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="text-align: left; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">We
obtain and update our understanding of the group, its activities, its control environment, and likely future developments, including
in relation to the legal and regulatory framework applicable and how the group is complying with that framework. Based on this understanding,
we identify and assess the risks of material misstatement of the financial statements, whether due to fraud or error, design and perform
audit procedures responsive to those risks, and obtain audit evidence that is sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for our opinion.
This includes consideration of the risk of acts by the entity that were contrary to applicable laws and regulations, including fraud.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; text-align: left; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">Based
on our understanding of the group, we identified that the principal risks of non-compliance with laws and regulations related to laws
and regulations that directly affect the financial statements including financial reporting legislation (including related companies
legislation), distributable profits legislation, pension legislation and UK tax legislation. In addition, the group is subject to many
other laws and regulations where the consequences of non-compliance could have a material effect on amounts or disclosures in the financial
statements, for instance through the imposition of fines and litigation. We considered the extent to which non-compliance with laws and
regulations might have a material effect on the financial statements and we have assessed the extent of compliance with these laws and
regulations as part of our procedures on the related financial statement items.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; text-align: left; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">We
also evaluated managements&rsquo; incentives and opportunities for fraudulent manipulation of the financial statements (including the
risk of override of controls) and determined that the principal risks related to posting inappropriate journal entries to manipulate
financial results, management bias in accounting estimates, as well as improper revenue recognition which includes fraudulent posting
of journal entries to revenue.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; text-align: left; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; text-align: left; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">Audit
procedures performed by the engagement team included:</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; text-align: left; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; text-align: justify; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">Because
of the inherent limitations of an audit, there is a risk that we will not detect all irregularities, including those leading to a material
misstatement in the financial statements or non-compliance with regulation. This risk increases the more that compliance with a law or
regulation is removed from the events and transactions reflected in the financial statements, as we will be less likely to become aware
of instances of non-compliance. The risk is also greater regarding irregularities occurring due to fraud rather than error, as fraud
involves intentional concealment, forgery, collusion, omission or misrepresentation.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top: 0pt; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; text-align: justify; margin-bottom: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">GeoPura
Ltd is a company limited by shares incorporated in England and Wales. The registered office is c/o Hobsons, Alexandra Street, Nottingham,
NG5 1AY. The company&rsquo;s registered number is 11855286. The principal activities are to deliver hydrogen-fuelled clean and sustainable
energy to replace diesel generators and decarbonise customers in off-grid and grid augmentation situations. The company achieves this
through an &lsquo;energy as a service&rsquo; business model: leasing its HPUs (Hydrogen Power Units) to customers with a GeoPura engineer backed
service delivery and full fuel management system to provide regular hydrogen supply. The company has one wholly-owned subsidiary, GeoPura
(Europe) ApS, incorporated in Denmark on 31 July 2025; these consolidated financial statements present the results and financial position
of the company and its subsidiary (together, the group).</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top: 0pt; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; text-align: justify; margin-bottom: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top: 0pt; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; text-align: justify; margin-bottom: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top: 0pt; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; text-align: justify; margin-bottom: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; text-align: justify; margin-bottom: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Basis

<P STYLE="margin-top: 0pt; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; color: #595959; text-align: justify; margin-bottom: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top: 0pt; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; text-align: justify; margin-bottom: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
consolidated financial statements incorporate the financial statements of the company and its wholly-owned subsidiary, GeoPura (Europe)
ApS, incorporated in Denmark. Subsidiaries are consolidated from the date on which control is obtained, and intra-group balances, transactions
and unrealised gains and losses are eliminated in full. GeoPura (Europe) ApS was incorporated during the year ended 31 March 2026 and
has been consolidated from incorporation; the comparative information and the opening IFRS statement of financial position at 1 April
2024 are therefore those of the company alone and are unaffected by consolidation.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top: 0pt; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; text-align: justify; margin-bottom: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top: 0pt; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; text-align: justify; margin-bottom: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
financial statements have been prepared on the historical cost basis, except for financial instruments measured at fair value through
profit or loss (IFRS 9) and share-based payment arrangements measured at grant-date fair value (IFRS 2). The financial statements are
presented in pounds sterling (&pound;), which is the functional and presentation currency of the company. The subsidiary&rsquo;s functional
currency is the Danish krone; its results and financial position are translated into sterling for consolidation. Unless otherwise stated,
amounts are rounded to the nearest thousand pounds (&pound;&rsquo;000), and totals may not cast exactly due to rounding.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top: 0pt; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; text-align: justify; margin-bottom: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top: 0pt; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; text-align: justify; margin-bottom: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
company presents assets and liabilities based on current and non-current classification. A liability is classified as current when it
is due to be settled within twelve months of the reporting date or there is no right to defer settlement for at least twelve months;
on this basis the convertible loan notes, which mature on 12 August 2026, are presented as current liabilities at 31 March 2026.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top: 0pt; font: 15pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-bottom: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 12pt"><B>Notes
to Consolidated Financial Statements (continued)</B></FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 4.65pt 0pt 5.05pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">Going
concern</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="color: #595959; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
company has been a wholly-owned subsidiary of Ballard Power Systems Inc. since 28 August 2026. Forecasts for at least twelve months from
approval show that capital expenditure and working capital depend on parent funding; Ballard has confirmed it will provide the support
needed to meet liabilities as they fall due. The financial statements are therefore prepared on the going concern basis.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 4.45pt 0pt 5.05pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">During
the year the company drew asset-backed and secured debt including facilities with Barclays and HSBC (bank borrowings at 31 March 2026:
&pound;31.5 million) and increased its convertible loan notes by &pound;27 million across the May and July 2025 tranches from existing
investors including Barclays Sustainable Impact Capital, General Motors Ventures, SWEN Capital Partners, Siemens Energy Ventures and
the National Wealth Fund.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 4.65pt 0pt 5.05pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">A
key consideration in the directors&rsquo; assessment is the convertible loan notes, the principal and accrued interest on which (&pound;98.7
million contractually at 31 March 2026; carrying amount &pound;113.2 million including the separated embedded derivative) (see note 33).</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 4.65pt 0pt 5.05pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">On
the basis of this assessment the directors continue to adopt the going concern basis in preparing these financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 4.7pt 0pt 5.05pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; width: 100%; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 0in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>3.</B></FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>New
                                            and forthcoming accounting standards</B></FONT></TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">As
first-time adoption of IFRS, all standards effective for periods beginning on or after 1 April 2025 have been applied from the date of
transition, including the amendments to IAS 1 (Classification of Liabilities as Current or Non-current; Non-current Liabilities with
Covenants), the amendments to IFRS 16 (Lease Liability in a Sale and Leaseback) and the amendments to IAS 21 (Lack of Exchangeability).
These are reflected in the accounting policies rather than disclosed as changes in accounting policy.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 4.5pt 0pt 5.05pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">Standards
issued but not yet effective which may be relevant to the company are: IFRS 18 Presentation and Disclosure in Financial Statements (effective
1 January 2027), which replaces IAS 1 and introduces defined subtotals and disclosure of management-defined performance measures, the
company is assessing its impact; and IFRS 19 Subsidiaries without Public Accountability: Disclosures (effective 1 January 2027), which
the company&rsquo;s Danish subsidiary may be eligible to apply in its own reporting. The company does not plan to adopt these standards
early.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 4.6pt 0pt 5.05pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
company&rsquo;s material accounting policies are set out below. These policies have been applied consistently to all periods presented
and in preparing the opening IFRS statement of financial position at 1 April 2024, except as explained in note 35.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 4.6pt 0pt 5.05pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">Revenue
from contracts with customers</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="color: #595959; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">Revenue
represents the consideration to which the company expects to be entitled in exchange for transferring goods and services to customers,
excluding value added tax, recognised by applying the five-step model in IFRS 15. The company has three principal revenue streams:</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 4.45pt 0pt 5.05pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Energy
as a Service</B>. The company supplies clean energy to customers through the hire of hydrogen power units (HPUs) together with engineer-backed
service delivery and a fuel management system providing hydrogen supply.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 4.65pt 0pt 5.05pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">Management
has assessed whether these arrangements contain a lease under IFRS 16 and concluded that they do not: although the customer obtains the
energy output, it is the company, rather than the customer, that directs the use of the HPUs, through its engineer-backed operation and
fuel management, and the company retains substantive rights to substitute units.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 4.5pt 0pt 5.05pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">Each
arrangement is accounted for within IFRS 15: HPU rental and service is a single performance obligation satisfied over time; hydrogen
supply is a distinct performance obligation for metered output, with variable consideration trued up to actual consumption; and separately
priced maintenance and delivery or haulage services are distinct performance obligations recognised as the services are provided.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 4.8pt 0pt 5.05pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 15pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-weight: normal">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; width: 100%"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">

<P STYLE="color: #666666; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0 0pt 5.05pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt"><B>Project
sales</B>. Revenue from the sale of hydrogen power units and hydrogen production equipment is recognised over time where the criteria
in IFRS 15 are met, in particular where the company&rsquo;s performance does not create an asset with an alternative use and the company
has an enforceable right to payment for performance completed to date, including through contractual termination-for-convenience compensation
providing cost plus a reasonable margin, using an input method to measure progress.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 4.6pt 0pt 5.05pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">Where
those criteria are not met, revenue is recognised at the point in time when control of the equipment transfers to the customer, assessed
with reference to title, physical possession, acceptance, and the transfer of significant risks and rewards.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 4.6pt 0pt 5.05pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">Joint
venture revenue</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="color: #595959; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">Revenue
from services provided to the HyMarnham Power joint venture is recognised as the services are performed. Revenue relating to the supply
of a production facility is recognised at a point in time when control of the facility transfers to the joint venture.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 4.45pt 0pt 5.05pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">Variable
consideration is included in the transaction price only to the extent that it is highly probable that a significant reversal will not
occur. Amounts invoiced in advance of performance are recognised as contract liabilities; amounts where performance precedes invoicing
are recognised as contract assets.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 4.9pt 0pt 5.05pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">Government
grants and other income</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="color: #595959; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">Government
grants, including funding associated with the Hydrogen Allocation Round, are recognised when there is reasonable assurance that the company
will comply with the conditions attaching to them and that the grants will be received.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 4.9pt 0pt 5.05pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">Leases</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="color: #595959; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">At
inception of a contract the company assesses whether the contract is, or contains, a lease. For each lease the company recognises a right-of-use
asset and a lease liability, except for short-term leases and leases of low-value assets, for which the lease payments are recognised
as an expense on a straight-line basis.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 4.55pt 0pt 5.05pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
lease liability is initially measured at the present value of the unpaid lease payments, discounted using the rate implicit in the lease
or, if that rate cannot be readily determined, the company&rsquo;s incremental borrowing rate; the right-of-use asset is initially measured
at cost and depreciated over the shorter of the lease term and the useful life of the asset, except where ownership transfers at the
end of the term (including hire purchase contracts), in which case the asset is depreciated over its useful life.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 4.7pt 0pt 5.05pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">Sale
and leaseback</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="color: #595959; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">Where
the company sells plant and leases it back under asset-backed financing arrangements, the company first assesses whether the transfer
is a sale under IFRS 15. Where control of the plant does not pass to the financier, as is the case for the company&rsquo;s finance-and-buy-back
arrangements, the transfer is not a sale: the plant continues to be recognised at its previous carrying amount and a financial liability
equal to the proceeds is recognised within borrowings and measured at amortised cost.</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 4.5pt 0pt 5.05pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">Property,
plant and equipment</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="color: #595959; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">Property,
plant and equipment is stated at cost less accumulated depreciation and accumulated impairment losses. Depreciation is provided to write
off the cost less estimated residual value over the estimated useful life of each asset:</FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin: 0pt 4.65pt 0pt 5.05pt; text-align: justify"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; font-size: 10pt">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; width: 100%"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<TD STYLE="width: 0in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in; text-align: left">4.</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Material accounting policies (continued)</TD>
</TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">Intangible assets and development
costs</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">Development expenditure is capitalised
as an intangible asset only when the IAS 38 criteria are demonstrated. Capitalised development expenditure is stated at cost less accumulated
amortisation and impairment; amortisation is charged on a straight-line basis over ten years from the date the asset is available for
use and is included within administrative expenses.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">Borrowing costs directly attributable
to qualifying assets are capitalised from the commencement of development where capitalisation commenced on or after 1 April 2024 (see
note 35).</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">Impairment of non-financial assets</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">At each reporting date the company
reviews the carrying amounts of its non-financial assets for indications of impairment; if any exist, the recoverable amount is estimated
as the higher of fair value less costs of disposal and value in use. Capitalised development expenditure not yet available for use is
tested annually.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">Inventories</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">Inventories are stated at the lower
of cost and net realisable value. Cost comprises the costs of purchase and, for units manufactured or assembled by the group, the direct
costs of bringing each unit to its present location and condition. Net realisable value is the estimated selling price in the ordinary
course of business less the estimated costs of completion and the estimated costs necessary to make the sale.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">Financial instruments</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">Financial assets and liabilities are recognised when the
group becomes party to the contractual provisions of the instrument.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="font: italic bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; width: 100%"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<TD STYLE="width: 0in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in; text-align: left">(i)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Classification</TD>
</TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">Financial assets are classified
as measured at amortised cost or at fair value through profit or loss (FVTPL). The classification depends on the business model for managing
the assets and on their contractual cash flows. Financial liabilities are measured at amortised cost, except derivatives, which are measured
at FVTPL. The group holds no instruments at fair value through other comprehensive income.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">Lease liabilities are measured under IFRS 16.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 12pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0"><B>GeoPura Ltd.</B></P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; width: 100%"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">

</TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="font: italic bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; width: 100%"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<TD STYLE="width: 0in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in; text-align: left">(ii)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Measurement</TD>
</TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify"><I>Amortised cost</I>: Financial
assets and liabilities at amortised cost are first measured at fair value. Directly attributable transaction costs are added for assets
and deducted for liabilities. Trade receivables without a significant financing component are first measured at the transaction price.
After that, these instruments are measured at amortised cost using the effective interest method. Financial assets are shown net of the
loss allowance.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify"><I>FVTPL</I>: Instruments at FVTPL
are first measured at fair value, and transaction costs are expensed. They are remeasured at fair value at each reporting date, and gains
and losses go to profit or loss.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify"><I>Convertible loan notes</I>: The
conversion feature does not meet the fixed-for-fixed condition in IAS 32. The conversion price varies with the pricing of a future funding
round, subject to a cap, and the class of shares delivered varies with the conversion event. The notes are therefore a financial liability
in full. The conversion triggers, the exit payoff and the noteholder put are separated from the host as a single compound embedded derivative.
At issue, the embedded derivative is measured at fair value. The host is measured as the residual of the proceeds, net of transaction
costs. The host is then measured at amortised cost using the effective interest method. The embedded derivative is remeasured at fair
value at each reporting date using a probability-weighted scenario model (note 30), and changes go to profit or loss. The host and the
embedded derivative are presented together within convertible loan notes.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="font: italic bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; width: 100%"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<TD STYLE="text-align: justify; width: 0in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in; text-align: justify">(iii)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Impairment of financial assets and contract assets</TD>
</TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">The group recognises a loss allowance
for ECL on financial assets at amortised cost and on contract assets. For trade receivables and contract assets, it applies the simplified
approach and measures the allowance at lifetime ECL. For other financial assets, the allowance is 12-month ECL. If credit risk has increased
significantly since initial recognition, lifetime ECL is used instead. Movements in the allowance go to profit or loss.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="font: italic bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; width: 100%"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<TD STYLE="text-align: justify; width: 0in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in; text-align: justify">(iv)</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Derecognition</TD>
</TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify"><I>Financial assets: </I>A financial
asset is derecognised when the rights to its cash flows expire. It is also derecognised when the asset is transferred together with substantially
all the risks and rewards of ownership.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify"><I>Financial liabilities:</I> A
financial liability is derecognised when the obligation is discharged, cancelled or expires. If the terms are modified substantially,
the original liability is derecognised and a new liability is recognised at fair value. The difference between the carrying amount derecognised
and the consideration paid goes to profit or loss.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">Foreign currency</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">The functional and presentation
currency of the company is pounds sterling. Transactions in foreign currencies, including the company&rsquo;s euro-denominated lease and
its Danish krone balances, are translated at the spot rate at the date of the transaction; monetary assets and liabilities denominated
in foreign currencies are translated at the closing rate, with exchange differences recognised in profit or loss.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">Taxation</P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">The tax expense comprises current
and deferred tax. Research and development tax reliefs and credits are recognised when it is probable that they will be received. Deferred
tax is recognised on temporary differences between the carrying amounts of assets and liabilities and their tax bases; deferred tax assets
are recognised only to the extent that it is probable that future taxable profits will be available.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">Share-based payments</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">The company operates an equity-settled
Company Share Option Plan (CSOP) for employees. The grant-date fair value of awards is recognised as an employee expense over the vesting
period, with a corresponding increase in equity, adjusted for the number of awards expected to vest under non-market vesting conditions.
Where vesting accelerates, for example on a change of control under the scheme rules, the remaining unrecognised charge is recognised
at the acceleration date.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">Employee benefits, provisions, cash and share capital</P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">Short-term employee benefits are recognised as an expense
as the service is received; the company operates a defined contribution pension scheme.</P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">Provisions</P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">Provisions are recognised for present obligations arising
from past events where an outflow is probable and can be reliably estimated.</P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">Cash and cash equivalents</P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">Cash and cash equivalents comprise cash at bank and in hand
and short-term deposits of three months or less.</P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">Reserves</P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="text-align: justify; font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">Ordinary shares and Series A shares are classified as equity,
with incremental issue costs recognised as a deduction from equity.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; width: 100%"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top; text-align: justify">
<TD STYLE="width: 0in"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 0.25in; text-align: left">5.</TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">Critical accounting judgements and key sources of estimation
uncertainty</TD>
</TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">Significant judgements</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">Classification of the convertible
loan notes. The directors have assessed, under IAS 32, that the conversion feature does not meet the fixed-for-fixed condition, because
the conversion price varies with future funding-round pricing and the class of shares varies with the conversion event; the notes are
therefore a financial liability in full with a separated compound embedded derivative.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">Sale and leaseback. The directors
have concluded that the asset-backed financing transactions entered into during the years ended 31 March 2025 and 31 March 2026 do not
transfer control of the plant and are accounted for as secured borrowings.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">Capitalisation of development expenditure.
The directors assess whether development projects, including the HPU 2, meet the IAS 38 capitalisation criteria.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">Key sources of estimation uncertainty</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">Fair value of the embedded derivative
within the convertible loan notes: measured using a probability-weighted scenario model with unobservable inputs, including the probabilities
of pre-maturity conversion, maturity conversion and exit events, calibrated to third-party market interest rate quotes at issue.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">Fair value of share-based payment
awards: the grant-date fair value of the CSOP options is measured using a Black-Scholes model, with the share value at each grant date
taken from contemporaneous funding-round pricing (&pound;50.54-&pound;185.00 per share) and expected volatility of 50-52%.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

and sub-debt and advanced &pound;27.0 million of loans, and the venture began production; its results are equity accounted from then (note

cost method for other inventory items. Net realisable value represents the estimated selling price less estimated costs of completion
and costs necessary to make the sale.</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">Bank and other loans</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">Bank and other loans
comprise facilities with Barclays (&pound;28.1 million) and HSBC (&pound;3.4 million, including an asset loan of &pound;4.7 million
original principal repayable in monthly instalments to September 2029 secured over plant), together with a Bounce Back Loan. The
obligations arising on the asset-backed financing transactions described below are presented within borrowings as secured borrowings
(2026: &pound;14.7 million; 2025: &pound;10.7 million); the H2 Production Doncaster facility is presented within lease liabilities
(note 24). The current portions of the bank loans are the instalments contractually due within twelve months: at 31 March 2026,
&pound;5.1 million on the Barclays facility (&pound;27 million drawn November 2025, semi-annual repayments from September 2026,
maturing March 2032) and &pound;0.9m on the HSBC asset loan, together with the residual Bounce Back Loan; at 31 March 2025,
&pound;1.1 million on the HSBC asset loan and the Bounce Back Loan instalment. The Eurotainer sale-and-hire-back is repayable by
monthly instalments of EUR 40.950k to December 2040 (undiscounted &pound;6.3 million at the transaction rate), secured on the 10
MEGC trailers concerned.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">Asset-backed financing arrangements</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">During the year ended 31 March 2025
the company entered into four sale-and-hire-purchase-back transactions, with Siemens Financial Services, Close Brothers (two arrangements)
and BNP Paribas, for proceeds of &pound;11,996k. During the year ended 31 March 2026 it entered into two further arrangements, with Siemens
Financial Services and Close Brothers, for proceeds of &pound;8,692k. In December 2025 the company also transferred 10 MEGC trailers to
Eurotainer for EUR 3.4 million and hired them back for 15 years; title and control were retained, so the proceeds are a secured borrowing
within long-term debt and the trailers remain in property, plant and equipment. Control of the plant did not pass to the financiers and
none of the transfers is a sale under IFRS 15: the plant continues to be recognised within property, plant and equipment and the proceeds
are recognised as secured borrowings measured at amortised cost.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">Convertible loan notes</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">The convertible loan notes comprise
three tranches: &pound;56 million issued in February 2024 at 14%, &pound;16 million issued in May 2025 at 16% and &pound;11 million issued
in July 2025 at 18% - &pound;83 million principal in aggregate. Interest accrues and rolls up from issue; unless converted, the principal
and accrued interest are due on 12 August 2026, and the notes are accordingly presented as current liabilities at 31 March 2026. The contractual
balance at 31 March 2026 of &pound;98.7 million comprises the &pound;83 million principal and accrued interest, less unamortised arrangement
fees. The carrying amount comprises the host liability at amortised cost of &pound;101.5 million (2025: &pound;61.2 million) and the embedded
derivative at fair value of &pound;11.7 million (2025: &pound;1.4 million) - see notes 30 and 35. The notes are classified as current
at 31 March 2026, as the 12 August 2026 maturity falls within twelve months of the reporting date; at 31 March 2025 and 1 April 2024 they
are classified as non-current, consistent with their contractual maturity at those dates.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">The notes convert into shares on
a qualifying funding round, an exit event or at maturity. The conversion price varies, by reference to the lowest price of a future funding
round less a discount, subject to a cap, and the class of shares varies with the conversion event; the fixed-for-fixed condition in IAS
32 is therefore not met and the notes are a financial liability in full. On transition, the conversion triggers, the exit payoff and the
noteholder put are separated together as a single compound embedded derivative at fair value through profit or loss, and the host is measured
at amortised cost at effective interest rates calibrated to third-party market quotes at issue (14% notes: 15.5%; 2025 tranches: 18.1%).
The notes converted into 717,621 shares after the year end, see note 33 for more information.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">The company operates an equity-settled
Company Share Option Plan (CSOP). Options were granted under the CSOP over &pound;1.00 ordinary shares at an exercise price of &pound;24.45
per share on 20 October 2023 (41,573 options), 27 November 2023 (3,172 options), 22 July 2024 (14,807 options), 3 February 2026 (6,903
options) and 2 June 2026 (33,933 options). Options vest three years from the vesting-commencement date, subject to continued employment,
and have a ten-year contractual life; in practice exercise is expected on an exit event. Under the scheme rules, options become exercisable
in full, vested and unvested, on a change of control of the company.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">The awards were unvested at the
date of transition, so the IFRS 1 D2 exemption is not available and IFRS 2 is applied in full: the grant-date fair value, measured using
a Black-Scholes model, is recognised over each three-year vesting period, with a cumulative catch-up in opening retained earnings at 1
April 2024 and charges in each of FY25 and FY26. For the June 2026 awards, employees began rendering services from the vesting-commencement
date of 25 February 2026, before the legal grant date; the charge is therefore recognised from that date based on an estimate of the grant-date
fair value. The February 2026 awards are recognised from their grant date, which is also their vesting-commencement date. Both awards
are included in the movements below. The announced acquisition of the company (note 33) would accelerate the residual unvested charge
into FY27.</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">Credit risk</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">The company applies the IFRS 9
simplified approach, measuring lifetime expected credit losses on trade receivables and contract assets. Expected credit losses are not
material at any date presented; the principal other receivables are capital equipment deposits and the euro reserve account, which the
directors assess for recoverability by reference to the counterparties and the underlying projects.</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">Market risk</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">The company is exposed to interest
rate risk on floating-rate borrowings, and to foreign currency risk principally on its euro-denominated lease and contract balances and
its Danish krone balances with the subsidiary. The fair value of the embedded derivative within the convertible loan notes is exposed
to changes in the probability and pricing of the conversion scenarios. The estimated effect on the loss before tax of reasonably possible
changes in each risk variable, with all other variables held constant, is:</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">Capital management</P>

<P STYLE="font: bold 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify">The company manages its capital
to ensure it can continue as a going concern while funding the growth of the HPU fleet, monitoring net debt (borrowings and lease liabilities
less cash) against equity. The capital structure at 31 March 2026 comprised net debt of &pound;156.8 million and net liabilities of &pound;46.3
million, reflecting the classification of the convertible loan notes as debt pending their expected conversion.</P>
